title: A Private Conversation

narrative.text: After the cabinet meeting, Vael requests a private word. He leads you to his study, closes the door, and pours two glasses of Arcturian whiskey. His manner is warm, avuncular, and utterly calculated.

Chancellor. I wanted to thank you personally for the Kravenstal contract. My consortium will deliver excellent work. As a gesture of appreciation — purely personal, not political — I have arranged for a consulting fee to be deposited in an account I have set up. Three thousand ₭. A small token. The account is in Morivask — entirely private. No one needs to know. Consider it a... bonus for good governance.

monologue: Three thousand ₭. 'A bonus for good governance.' He said it with a straight face. The account is in Morivask — Vael's preferred jurisdiction for things that cannot be explained in a budget committee. The whiskey is the same vintage every time, which means he has a case of it. A case of whiskey ready for every corrupt conversation he expects to have. The scale of the preparation is the warning.

choices.text: "I... appreciate the gesture, Vael." (Accept the 3,000 ₭ kickback. Your personal wealth increases. But this is corruption — it will be recorded. If it ever comes to light, the consequences will be severe.)

reactions.text: He slides a small envelope across the desk — account details, Morivask bank, no name. He does not smile. Professionals at this level do not smile. He simply makes a note in his ledger.

choices.text: "Vael, I gave you the contract because you were the best bid — not because I wanted a personal relationship. Keep your consulting fee. Build the steelworks. That is all I want from you."

reactions.text: He sets down his glass. The whiskey is untouched. He does not argue. The silence is the sound of a man who has just been told no and is recalculating.
